title: Proper native Weil direct image finiteness on the constructible heart
statement:
Fix a finite field $k_0$ and a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k_0)$. Use the locally finite continuous $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ coefficient sheaves, the categories $\mathcal A_T$ of their module sheaves, the categories $\mathcal W_T$ of pro-etale sheaves with invertible Frobenius structure, and the constructibility condition of [def-sf-native-weil-derived-framework]. Let $p:Z\to T$ be a proper morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism] of $k_0$-schemes, with $T$ quasi-compact, quasi-separated [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism] and locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] over $k_0$. The ordinary equivariant direct image $p_{0*}:\mathcal W_Z\to\mathcal W_T$ is additive and left exact. For each $F\in\mathcal W_Z$ with constructible underlying sheaf, place $F$ in degree zero in the ordinary derived category. Then the actual total right derived functor $Rp_{0*}$ of $p_{0*}$ satisfies
$$H^n(Rp_{0*}(F[0]))=0\quad\text{outside a finite integer interval},$$
and the underlying sheaf of $H^n(Rp_{0*}(F[0]))$ is constructible for every $n\in\mathbf Z$. This assertion concerns derivation in $\mathcal W_Z$, not fixed pairs in the derived category of $\mathcal A_Z$.

proof.text: Put $k=\overline{k_0}$ and write $\bar p:\bar Z\to\bar T$ for geometric base change. Properness survives this base change by [lem-pc-proper-base-change], hence $\bar p$ is quasi-compact and locally of finite type by the definition of properness, and quasi-separated by [lem-pc-separated-quasi-separated]. The structure morphism $\bar T\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is quasi-compact and locally of finite type by [lem-pc-quasi-compact-base-change] and [lem-weil-pbc-lft-base-change], applied to $T\to\operatorname{Spec}k_0$. Its quasi-compactness is precisely quasi-compactness of $T$, since the target has its single affine chart. Characteristic is unchanged by field extension: the field inclusion $k_0\hookrightarrow k$ has zero kernel, so a positive integer kills $1$ in one field exactly when it does in the other. Thus $\operatorname{char}k\ne\ell$.

proof.text: Write $G=\bar p_*$ for the ordinary module direct image and $U_S:\mathcal W_S\to\mathcal A_S$ for forgetting Frobenius. Kernels of module sheaves are sectionwise by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. By the direct-image definition of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], on a pro-etale test object $V\to\bar T$, $(GM)(V)=M(V\times_{\bar T}\bar Z)$, with scalars restricted along the coefficient map of [def-sf-native-weil-derived-framework]. Consequently $G(a+b)=G(a)+G(b)$, $G(0)=0$, and $G(\ker a)=\ker(Ga)$: all three are the same equalities evaluated at $V\times_{\bar T}\bar Z$. Frobenius is an automorphism; [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image] identifies its pullback with an equivalence of sites. The coefficient identification is literally precomposition of the same locally finite functions, whose inverse is precomposition by the inverse automorphism. Hence Frobenius acts by additive autoequivalences on these module categories. The lifted direct image has underlying functor $G$ and structure $G(\phi)\circ c_M$ by the framework definition. The kernel of a commuting map carries the restriction of this invertible structure, because the Frobenius equivalence preserves kernels; finite direct sums carry the sum structure. Therefore the displayed sectionwise equalities lift to $p_{0*}$, proving its additivity and left exactness.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-adic-affine-direct-image-finiteness] over $k$ to every pair of affine schemes occurring in the affine hypothesis of [lem-sf-adic-affine-finiteness-descent]. The coefficient models agree: locally finite-dimensional $\mathbf Q_\ell$-span implies values in a finite extension, because a basis consists of finitely many elements of the algebraic closure and their compositum is finite; conversely values in a finite extension have finite-dimensional span. Both constructibility conditions mean finite locally closed constructible stratifications locally on the scheme, with finite free trivializations on pro-etale covers. No common-stage pair category is substituted for these module categories. The affine hypothesis is therefore satisfied. The descent lemma, with $f=\bar p$ and the geometric hypotheses from step 1, gives bounded constructible $R\bar p_*((U_ZF)[0])$, since the single complex has only its degree-zero cohomology $U_ZF$.

proof.text:
The categories $\mathcal A_S$ are categories of modules over the actual ring sheaf $B_{\bar S}$ on the small pro-etale site; they are Grothendieck abelian by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck], in a common sheaf-value universe. Apply [lem-sf-fixed-pair-derived-forget-comparison] to these categories, their Frobenius autoequivalences verified in step 2, the additive left exact functor $G$, and the natural Frobenius comparison $c$ supplied in [def-sf-native-weil-derived-framework]. Its transported functor is exactly $p_{0*}$ by the formula in step 2. The lemma gives the canonical isomorphism in the ordinary underlying derived category
$$D(U_T)Rp_{0*}(F[0])\xrightarrow{\sim}R\bar p_*((U_ZF)[0]).$$
In particular this is a comparison of the actual right derived functors: it does not replace $D(\mathcal W)$ by fixed pairs in $D(\mathcal A)$.

proof.text: Let $C=Rp_{0*}(F[0])$. The fixed-pair comparison lemma says that $U_T$ is exact and conservative. Exactness identifies $U_TH^n(C)$ with $H^n(D(U_T)C)$: applying $U_T$ to $\ker d^n/\operatorname{im}d^{n-1}$ preserves both the kernel and its quotient. Taking cohomology of step 4 identifies this with $H^n(R\bar p_*((U_ZF)[0]))$. Step 3 supplies an interval $[a,b]$ outside which the latter is zero, and constructibility in every degree. For $n\notin[a,b]$, $U_T(0\to H^n(C))$ is an isomorphism, so conservativity makes $0\to H^n(C)$ an isomorphism. Thus $C$ vanishes in those degrees. In every degree its underlying cohomology sheaf is isomorphic to the constructible sheaf from step 3 and is constructible by transporting the local finite-free trivializations. This proves both required finiteness clauses.
